lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Give one affirm and one oppose reason for "Students should have a weekly outdoor learning afternoon."

FEEDBACK
Affirm: outdoor learning supports health and attention. Oppose: wet weather and planning time can make it hard every week.

CHECK
Winning is not the only goal; clear reasons and fair turn-taking matter.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Hold a short structured debate (two speakers each side or roles with a parent). Prepare two reasons each, speak for up to 45 seconds per turn, and write one fair point you heard from the other side.

Write a short reflection describing one specific revision you made and why.
lesson.learning_intention: A simple debate has a clear topic, speakers who affirm or oppose, reasons with examples, and respectful listening.
lesson.offline_alternative: Use paper and pencil to complete the original task, then retain a photograph or short parent observation as evidence.
lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Hold a short structured debate (two speakers each side or roles with a parent). Prepare two reasons each, speak for up to 45 seconds per turn, and write one fair point you heard from the other side. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Original response on new material: Affirm: outdoor learning supports health and attention. Oppose: wet weather and planning time can make it hard every week. Reasoning: I used debate by attending to affirm and explain why it matters rather than copying the worked model.

Parent: Written model 2: Common error: Winning is not the only goal; clear reasons and fair turn-taking matter. Correction: Affirm: outdoor learning supports health and attention. Oppose: wet weather and planning time can make it hard every week. Why: the correction restores accurate use of debate.

Parent: Likely misconception: Winning is not the only goal; clear reasons and fair turn-taking matter. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Produce a fresh example demonstrating debate on new material (not the worked model). Explain the particular words, sources or choices that make it work.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one likely error with debate, correct it, and explain why the correction helps a reader or audience.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Topic: "School days should start later." Affirm reason: more sleep helps concentration. Oppose reason: later finishes reduce daylight sport time. Speakers take turns without interrupting.

TRY FIRST
Give one affirm and one oppose reason for "Students should have a weekly outdoor learning afternoon."

FEEDBACK
Affirm: outdoor learning supports health and attention. Oppose: wet weather and planning time can make it hard every week.
teach_steps.explain:
A simple debate has a clear topic, speakers who affirm or oppose, reasons with examples, and respectful listening.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make decisions based on specific language evidence, rather than guess or copy someone else. Keep the meaning accurate and explain the choice.

HOW TO WORK
Read the original example and locate the words or actions that support the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Check your response against the feedback: did you address the same skill and show your reasoning? If a detail is uncertain, identify what would have to be checked. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than making the answer longer.
teach_steps.notice: Winning is not the only goal; clear reasons and fair turn-taking matter. Correct the meaning, not just the appearance.
